parsed.explanation: The quoted sentence appears verbatim (modulo an ellipsis for '(since at most n cuts)') and the write-up itself frames it as a 'need', not a result. Checking the whole text: the subsequent discussion shows the equal-grid completion strategy fails when Liu's cuts are off-grid, says 'So need different Xiang strategy to upper bound,' then defers to an unexecuted computational search for n=2. No Xiang reply construction against an arbitrary Liu division is ever given for any n beyond the trivial grid-aligned case, and no cancellation/overlay or pigeonhole argument appears. Hence the all-n upper bound (obligation U) is nowhere established, exactly as the objection claims; optimality of the conjectured value is wholly unproved. Since (U) is a required component of a complete proof and is not repaired elsewhere, the gap is fatal to the upper-bound obligation.
